title: Crowd impact geometry final whole-scene evidence
status: valid controlled evidence; 60 FPS target remains unmet

conclusion.headless: Across the rotated six-run controlled comparison, the median of run means changed from 23.666 ms to 21.114 ms (-10.78%). All three candidate run means were lower, while one paired p95 comparison regressed; baseline temporal drift prevents a blanket tail claim.
conclusion.rendered: The paced GL Compatibility and Forward+ B/A/B rows do not show a stable whole-frame gain. GL rendering remains far above the 16.67 ms target, and the shipping renderer was not changed.
conclusion.scope: The controlled candidate combines the native cape, flight and world kernels, the cape capsule cache, and the retained ranger-bow local geometry. Focused tests isolate component correctness and callback cost; their savings are not added to scene timings.

worldEffect.caveat: Focused microbench reductions are not a whole-frame or 60 FPS claim.

rangerBow.conclusion: When exact local draw point and flex are unchanged, retaining bowstring geometry and cached limb nodes preserves reviewed output and reduces the complete equipped-bow update_pose callback by about 40-46% in the focused repeated-pose workload.

correctness.windowedExactParity: 19 actor presentation states plus 11-step dynamic bow sequence; zero failures
dynamicCases: idle world motion with retained local geometry

rangerBow.postRunNormalization: The frozen bow fixture final file removes one trailing blank line and the probe updates that file-hash constant. The frozen pose function bytes and runtime semantics are unchanged; per-session manifests retain the exact measured file hashes.

smokes.capeCensusExplanation: The mixed fixture has 150 equipped humanoids. A total of 180 actors expose cape-compatible SkeletonModifier3D nodes, but only the 150 worn/configured capes initialize native kernels. The other 30 dormant, unworn modifiers retain the default gdscript backend label. Native cape calls remain 75 per sampled frame.

visualReview.finding: Reviewed GL and Forward+ baseline/candidate active and settled views retained dense two-band crowds, creature/equipped-humanoid identity, overhead labels, health bars and live effects. No obvious missing geometry or equipment was seen.
visualReview.limitations: Captures are asynchronous and are not pixel or animation parity evidence. Forward+ ground remained brighter and effects paler than GL in baseline and candidate; this pre-existing renderer difference still needs broader art QA.
